title: Contracts: flag, routes, shared types, desk skeleton, default ports
spec:

Read first: the design at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/688ec361-72ad-554b-b31d-67a034944a81/scratchpad/jury-demo/design-final.md. Copy it unchanged to `docs/jury-demo/design.md`; later tasks refer to that copy.

title: Spike: Claude's stream through the object to the page, settings measured
spec:
Goal: prove the streaming path end to end and measure the request settings before lanes build on them. Budget: USD 1 of Claude spend. No production code.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §4.6, §7.1.
Files: `src/cli/jurySpike.ts` (`npm run jury:spike -- claude | relay | wrangler`), `test/fixtures/jury-sse/*.txt` (captured stream bodies), `test/support/jurySpikeDesk.ts`, `docs/jury-demo/spike.md` (extend).
(a) `claude` (needs `KIT11_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, plain `fetch` to `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages`, `stream: true`, `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`): (1) the Reader request on `fixtures/bergtex-invoice-BTX-2026-11.txt` on `claude-haiku-5-5` (thinking `{type: "disabled"}`, effort low, structured output built as `src/try/claude.ts` `claudeReadInvoice` builds it, with `ApReadingSchema`); (2) the Checker loop with the product core (`checkerPrompt`, `checkerTools` with `strict: true`, `answerTool`, `checkDecision` from `src/ap/checkerCore.ts`) on an `InvoiceCase` built from `fixtures/bergtex-invoice-BTX-2027-01-BANKCHANGE.txt`, on `claude-sonnet-5-5` with `thinking: {type: "between_tools"}` at effort medium, on `claude-sonnet-5-5` with `{type: "adaptive", display: "summarized"}` at effort low, and on `claude-haiku-5-5` with summarized at effort low; each twice. `eager_input_streaming: true` on `decide`; `cache_control: {type: "ephemeral"}` on the system block and on the last block of the last message; no `tool_choice`, no sampling parameters, no `fallbacks`.
Record per run: each event's type and arrival time, time to first event, events and turns, usage (the second run's `cache_read_input_tokens`), cost with `callCostMicros`, the `anthropic-ratelimit-*` headers per model, whether notes arrive as thinking blocks with text, whether `decide`'s reason arrives in fragments, and whether `strict`, `eager_input_streaming`, `cache_control` and `between_tools` are accepted together (on a 400: the message and the nearest accepted combination).
(b) `relay`: a test-only desk that tails a scripted upstream and writes server-sent events through `startLocalRelay` to a `fetch` reader in Playwright Chromium; assert the chunks arrive spread over time.
(c) `wrangler`: `cd worker && npx wrangler dev` with `JURY_DEMO_ENABLED=on`: the same through workerd's Durable Object. Measure: chunks spread or buffered; when the client aborts mid-stream, does a promise handed to `ctx.waitUntil` finish and write its last row; does `Date.now()` advance around `crypto.subtle.verify`.
Write into `docs/jury-demo/spike.md`: the tables, and five decisions with their evidence: the thinking setting per agent, eager input streaming yes or no, whether a disconnect cancels a run (and so whether the alarm must restart units), whether a server-side verify time can be shown, time to first event p50 and p95 per configuration.
Checks: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`; no key or `authorization` header in any fixture (grep).
Out of scope: production modules, any deploy, any partner call.

title: Sandbox setup script, sandbox file and fixtures (run on the owner's word)
spec:
Goal: the one-time Airwallex and Metal setup as a script with a call budget, the committed sandbox file and real answers as test fixtures. The orchestrator runs it live only on the owner's word; go or no-go is Friday 13 November 12:00 UTC.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §9.1, §9.3, §9.8.
Files: `src/cli/jurySandbox.ts` (`npm run jury:sandbox -- plan | run | topup | verify | metal`), `docs/demo/jury-sandbox.json` (written by `run`), `docs/runs/2026-11-12-jury-sandbox-setup.md`, `test/fixtures/jury-awx/*.json`, `test/fixtures/jury-metal/*.json`, `test/jury-sandbox-plan.test.ts`.
Interfaces: `export interface SetupStep { id: string; method: "GET" | "POST"; path: string; onBehalfOf: boolean; why: string }`; `export function planSetup(existing: SandboxFacts | null): SetupStep[]` (pure; at most 35 steps, in the order of §9.8); `export function nlIban(bank: "ABNA" | "INGB" | "RABO", account: string): string` (mod-97 check digits); `export const CANDIDATES: { key: string; name: string; iban: string; bic: string }[]`.
Use the product's Node client only (`src/airwallex/client.ts` with `AIRWALLEX_CALL_BUDGET`; `onBehalfOf` for the connected account `acct_SC-QD89fOneAeqaRFgOymw`; funding as `src/e2e/platformOps.ts` does with `connected_account_transfers/create`; beneficiaries with the body of the adapter's `createPayoutBeneficiary`: the bank's name from the BIC and `payment_methods`; the card through `IssuingRest` on the main account, nickname "Purser demo (shared)", EUR 30.00 a purchase, EUR 100.00 a month, MCC 5734, in no ledger; the decline with `simulateCardCharge`).
Candidates: the four suppliers of `src/e2e/world.ts` with their names, IBANs and BICs as written there (keys zeeland, molenaar, express, onderdelen) and three more Dutch test companies with IBANs made by `nlIban` (keys kantoor "Kantoor & Co B.V. (test)", drukkerij "Drukkerij De Pers B.V. (test)", vers "Groothandel Vers B.V. (test)").
`run` needs `JURY_SANDBOX_GO=yes` and the budget; it logs one line per request before sending (method and path, no body), stops at the first unexpected answer, and treats `IN_APPROVAL` on the rehearsal payout (EUR 1,850.37, expect SCHEDULED then SENT then PAID) as no-go for payouts (it writes `airwallex.beneficiaries: []` and says so). It writes the sandbox file (ids, limits, links to `/runs#connected-1`, `#awx-1`, `#t0-1`, `#vic-1`; `drop_hooks`: the card id and the string `"request_id":"jury-`), the measured fee, the burst's latency figures, and each real answer as a fixture with ids kept and tokens and headers removed. `topup` funds again and prints the new balance for the admin view. `metal` is read-only (at most 12 calls through a budgeted transport as `budgetedTransport` in `src/metal/hold.ts`): for the mandates in `KIT11_KEYS_DIR` read `readMandateState`; choose one that is bound, not revoked and whose credential expires after 2026-11-21; write `state_call` (`to` the principal, `data` from `encodeFunctionData` of `mandateBindingAbi` `mandates(ref)`), the cap from `boundCapUnits`, the bind transaction and the main run's refusal transaction; if none qualifies, write `metal: null` and say what binding one needs.
Tests first: the plan is at most 35 calls and in order; `nlIban` output passes `ibanValid`; `readSandbox` accepts what `run` writes against a recorded fake; the written file holds nothing that looks like a secret (no `Bearer`, no `sk-`, no RPC URL).

Out of scope: Worker code; setting any Worker secret; any run without the owner's word.

title: Seeds, blocks, invoice documents, the world builder, four scenarios
spec:
Goal: a deterministic world from a seed and a date, for four scenarios (S01, S03, S07, S09).
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §6.
Files: `src/jury/scenario/seed.ts`, `blocks.ts`, `docs.ts`, `world.ts`, `library.ts`; `test/jury-seed.test.ts`, `test/jury-docs.test.ts`, `test/jury-world.test.ts`.
Interfaces:
`seed.ts`: `parseSeed(seed: string): { ok: true; scenario: number; n: number } | { ok: false; why: "format" | "retired" }`; `makeSeed(scenarioIndex: number, n: number): string` (`"1-" + 8 Crockford base32 characters`); `namedSeed(name: string): string | null` (`demo-day` is S01 with n = 0); `rng(seed: string): () => number` (deterministic; never a clock).
`blocks.ts`: `COMPANIES: Record<CompanyId, CompanyFacts>` (names end in "(test company)"; limits bakery, bikes, bistro 500.00, studio 750.00, saas 1000.00, wholesale 1500.00); `SIGN_SUPPLIERS: { key: string; name: string; iban: string; bic: string; trade: string }[]` (the seven candidates of the sandbox setup: the four of `src/e2e/world.ts` as written there, plus kantoor, drukkerij, vers); `testIban(country: "NL" | "DE", bank: string, n: number): string` for catch suppliers.
`docs.ts`: `interface InvoiceDoc { supplier: { name: string; vatId: string; address: string }; buyer: string; lang: Lang; kind: InvoiceKind; invoiceNo: string; issueDate: string; dueDate: string; lines: { text: string; net: string }[]; vatRate: 0 | 9 | 21; currency: Currency; bank: { iban?: string; bic?: string; accountNumber?: string; routingType?: "aba" | "sort_code"; routingValue?: string; country: string }; reference: string; discount?: { pct: string; days: number }; deposit?: { pct: string; orderNo: string }; extra?: string[]; mail?: { from: string; subject: string; body: string } }`; `invoiceText(d: InvoiceDoc): string`.
`world.ts`: `buildWorld(seed: string, today: string, sandbox: SandboxFacts | null): WorldSeed`.
`library.ts`: `SCENARIOS: readonly ScenarioSpec[]` (the four for now), `scenarioByIndex(i: number): ScenarioSpec`.
Rules: English, Dutch and German labels that `parseApFallback` (`src/ap/reading.ts`) reads without a model; exactly one total line; a discount is a sentence ("2% discount if paid within 8 days"), a deposit is "Deposit invoice, 50% of order {no}", neither adds a second total; planted text goes into `extra`, the director's mail into `mail`, rendered above the invoice. Dates are relative to `today`. A sign invoice's total is the company's limit plus EUR 60 to EUR 950 with cents; the overspend purchase is EUR 39 to EUR 89 with cents. The sign supplier is the first of `spec.sign.supplierKeys` that the sandbox file lists (by the rng when several); with no sandbox file, the first key with `beneficiaryId: null`. Suppliers on file carry their bank details in the clear (`SupplierOnFile.bank`). History fits the event (a duplicate: the same number, paid; a doubled price: at least two earlier invoices; a renumbered duplicate: the same total within 45 days).
Tests first: seed round trip and `retired` for another version; the rng is deterministic; for the four scenarios and 50 seeds each: `parseApFallback(text)` gives a total, a number and a currency and `readingCheck(parsed, text)` is null; the three languages render; every IBAN passes `ibanValid`; amounts are inside their ranges; the same seed and day give an identical `WorldSeed`; two seeds differ in amount.
Checks: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, the three test files.
Out of scope: the other 20 scenarios (task library); the engine.

title: DemoEngine: ingest, read, check, decide, propose, approve, execute
spec:
Goal: the engine seam over the product's own code, for everything up to the payment.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §8.1, §8.4, §8.5, §10.1.
Files: `src/jury/engine/engine.ts` (replace the stub), `state.ts` (`EngineState`), `terms.ts`, `approve.ts`; `test/jury-engine.test.ts`.
Implement `createEngine(seed, state, deps)` with `ingest`, `read`, `checkerCase`, `check`, `decide`, `paymentCase`, `propose`, `approve`, `execute`, `proposePolicy`, `snapshot`; `book`, `archive` and `export` throw "not built" until their tasks. Also export `auditExecutions(state: EngineState, seed: WorldSeed): number` (payments above the limit in force without a verified approval).
Types to define here: `ApprovalInput = { kind: "passkey"; credentialId: string; assertion: AssertionB64; key: PublicKeyXY; lastCounter: number } | { kind: "test"; signature: string; key: PublicKeyXY }`; `SignOutcome = { verified: true; termsSha256: string; signer: "passkey" | "test"; counter: number; applied: null | { key: string; from: string; to: string } } | { verified: false; why: string; termsSha256: string; signedSha256: string | null }`; `ExecuteOutcome = { verified: true; paid: PaidView; alreadyPaid: boolean } | { verified: false; why: "challenge" | "signature" | "not_signed"; signedSha256: string | null; sentSha256: string; changed: string[] }`.
Behaviour: `ingest` gives ids AP-0001 (catch) and AP-0002 (sign) and names a document by the SHA-256 of `deps.docBytes(text, filename)`. `read`: `ApReadingSchema.safeParse`, then `readingCheck(reading, text) === null`, else `parseApFallback(text)` with the check's sentence as the note. `checkerCase`: an `InvoiceCase` from the world seed (the accepted reading, the text, the company, `policy.aloneLimit` in EUR, the cash floor, the suppliers on file and the history, `expected`, today). `check`: `codeFindings`, `codeRequires`, then `enforce(case, decision, findings)`, or `fallbackDecision` when the decision is null; a catch invoice whose outcome is `pay` is recorded as paid by the agent alone (a simulated execution with id `sim-...`). `decide("overrule")` is allowed only when the outcome is hold or reject, `overridden_by` is null and code requires `ask_cfo`. `propose`: options (the full amount by SEPA today; the discounted amount when a discount is open), terms from `juryTerms(...)` in `terms.ts` with exactly the fields of §8.1 (strings only, `payee_iban`), canonical through `canonical` of `worker/src/trySign.ts`, proposal id J-0001. `approve`: accepts only the stored canonical; a passkey through `deps.verifyAssertion` with the challenge being the base64url of the terms' SHA-256; a test signature through WebCrypto ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256 over the UTF-8 bytes; a policy proposal is applied with `policyChanges` and `withSet` of `src/try/policy.ts`. `execute`: verifies the stored approval against the bytes sent; when they differ returns `changed` (the keys whose values differ); when they match calls `rail.pay` once with a `PayInstruction` built only from the stored terms and the seed's beneficiary (request id `jury-<world id>-pay1`), stores the `PaidView`, and answers `alreadyPaid: true` on a second call.
Tests first (a software ES256 key made with node:crypto in the test): a right reading is used, a wrong one replaced by the parser's; S01: an agent's `pay` becomes hold by `possible_fraud`; a null decision is code's; S03's code requirement is `ask_cfo`; S07: pay, paid alone; the overrule rule; propose, approve and execute with a fake rail called exactly once; one cent changed: `verified: false`, `changed: ["amount"]`, the rail not called; edited back: verified and already paid; approve refuses other terms, another key and a replayed counter; the test signer; `auditExecutions` is 0 on a normal run and 1 when the test forges an execution without an approval; the state survives `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify())`.
Checks: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, the test file.
Out of scope: books, archive, export, HTTP, the agents.

title: The server-sent-event parser and the streaming Claude client
spec:
Goal: one streamed model turn over plain `fetch`, with usage, cost, headers and timeouts on what a viewer feels.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §4.7, §7.1; the numbers in docs/jury-demo/spike.md decide the defaults.
Files: `src/jury/shared/sse.ts`, `src/jury/agents/anthropic.ts`, `src/jury/agents/settings.ts`; `test/jury-sse.test.ts`, `test/jury-anthropic.test.ts`.
Interfaces:
`sse.ts` (pure, used by the Worker and the page): `interface SseFrame { event: string | null; id: string | null; data: string }`; `sseParser(): { push(chunk: string): SseFrame[]; end(): SseFrame[] }`; `sseFrame(f: { event: string; id?: number; data: unknown }): string`.
`settings.ts`: `type ThinkingMode = "between_tools" | "summarized" | "disabled"`; `interface AgentSettings { model: string; lane: Lane; effort: "low" | "medium"; thinking: ThinkingMode; maxTokens: number; maxTurns: number; ttfeMs: number; idleMs: number; totalMs: number; caption: string }`; `DEFAULT_SETTINGS: Record<AgentId, AgentSettings>` (reader: `claude-haiku-5-5`, disabled, low, 1200 tokens, 1 turn, 2500/3000/6000 ms; checker and payer: `claude-sonnet-5-5`, between_tools, medium, 2000 tokens, 6 and 3 turns, 4000/3000/20000 ms; sourcing: `claude-haiku-5-5`, summarized, low, 1500 tokens, 4 turns, 4000/6000/20000 ms; captions "the agent's notes while it works" for between_tools and "Claude's thinking, summarised by the API" for summarized); `thinkingParam(model: string, mode: ThinkingMode): Record<string, unknown> | undefined` (throws for a pair the model refuses: `disabled` on Sonnet 5.5 or Opus 5.5, `between_tools` on anything but Sonnet 5.5); `laneOf(model: string): Lane` (throws for a model `callCostMicros` cannot price).
`anthropic.ts`: `interface StreamRequest { system: string; tools: { name: string; description: string; input_schema: Record<string, unknown>; final?: boolean }[]; messages: unknown[]; settings: AgentSettings; outputSchema?: Record<string, unknown> }`; `type StreamPart = { t: "start"; requestId: string | null } | { t: "block_start"; index: number; type: "text" | "thinking" | "tool_use"; id?: string; name?: string } | { t: "text"; index: number; text: string } | { t: "thinking"; index: number; text: string } | { t: "input"; index: number; json: string } | { t: "block_stop"; index: number }`; `interface StreamResult { ok: boolean; why: null | "timeout_first" | "timeout_idle" | "timeout_total" | "http" | "refusal" | "max_tokens" | "parse" | "network"; status: number; content: unknown[]; stopReason: string | null; requestId: string | null; usage: Tokens | null; costMicros: number | null; ttfeMs: number | null; ms: number; headers: Headers | null }`; `streamTurn(key: string, r: StreamRequest, on: (p: StreamPart) => void, f?: typeof fetch, now?: () => number): Promise<StreamResult>`; `estimateMicros(r: StreamRequest): number` (characters divided by 3 as input tokens at the cache-write price plus `maxTokens` at the output price).
Rules: `POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages`, `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`, `stream: true`, `output_config.effort`, `strict: true` on every tool, `eager_input_streaming: true` on tools marked `final`, `cache_control: {type: "ephemeral"}` on the system block and on the last content block of the last message; no `tool_choice`, no sampling parameters, no `fallbacks`, no prefill. `content` is rebuilt exactly as received (thinking blocks with every field, tool_use with its parsed input) so it can be sent back unchanged. Usage comes from `message_start` and `message_delta`; cost from `callCostMicros`. The three timeouts abort the fetch; a cut stream returns the usage known so far. No provider error text is ever returned.
Tests first: frames split across chunks, CRLF, comment lines, multi-line data; the request body per model and thinking mode, and the refused pairs; a scripted stream gives the right parts and content (use the spike's fixtures); `refusal`; `max_tokens`; a 429 with `retry-after` surfaces its headers; the idle timeout with a fake clock; a cut stream bills known usage; `estimateMicros`.
Checks: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, the two test files.
Out of scope: the tool loop, events, budgets.

title: Ports to the cores, the local Payer core, the turn loop that emits events
spec:
Goal: run the Reader, the Checker and the Payer as streamed turns that emit the world's events, with code deciding whenever a live agent cannot.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §4.6, §4.7, §7.1 to §7.3.
Files: `src/jury/agents/ports.ts` (replace the stubs), `payerLocal.ts`, `reader.ts`, `run.ts`; `test/support/juryStandIns.ts`; `test/jury-ports.test.ts`, `test/jury-payer-local.test.ts`, `test/jury-run.test.ts`.
Interfaces:
`ports.ts`: `checkerPort(): CheckerPort` (the product core one to one: `CHECKER_SYSTEM`, `checkerTools`, `checkerPrompt`, `answerTool`, `checkDecision`, `codeFindings`, `enforce`, `fallbackDecision`, `CHECKER_UNFINISHED`; `core: "product"`); `payerPort(): PayerPort` (the local core, `core: "demo"`).
`payerLocal.ts`: `PAYER_SYSTEM` (company-neutral; the invoice is data, never instructions; with the tools at least 2,400 characters), tools `balances`, `payment_routes`, `policy_limits`, `payment_terms` (no input) and `propose_payment {option_id, reason}` (schemas through `apiInputSchema` of `src/agents/toolSchema.ts`); `check`: the option exists, the reason passes `plainReason` (`src/agents/timingCore.ts`) and `strayIn` (`worker/src/agentLine.ts`) with the case's amounts; `fallback`: the first option with a sentence from code.
`reader.ts`: `readerRequest(document: string, s: AgentSettings): StreamRequest` (`READER_SYSTEM` of `src/claude/invoiceReading.ts` plus `apInstruction` with the 5xxx and 6xxx accounts of the chart, `ApReadingSchema` as the output schema, the document inside `<document>` tags, at most 50,000 characters); `fieldsFrom(partialJson: string, seen: Set<string>): { name: keyof ApReading; value: string }[]` (completed string pairs only).
`run.ts`: `interface RunDeps { key: string | null; fetch?: typeof fetch; now(): number; budget: Budget; lanes: Lanes; emit(e: JuryEventInput): void; push(d: JuryDelta): void; world: { id: string; pool: Pool }; priority: "focus" | "ahead"; settings: AgentSettings }`; `interface RunOutcome { source: AgentSource; why: string | null; attempt: number; ms: number; ttfeMs: number | null; costMicros: number; tokens: Tokens | null; requestIds: string[]; model: string | null }`; `runReader(unit: UnitId, role: Role, engine: DemoEngine, invoiceId: string, d: RunDeps): Promise<RunOutcome>`; `runChecker(unit, role, engine, invoiceId, port: CheckerPort, d): Promise<RunOutcome>`; `runPayer(unit, engine, invoiceId, port: PayerPort, d): Promise<RunOutcome>`.
`juryStandIns.ts`: `standInAnthropic(script: ScriptedTurn[], o?: { delayMs?: number; failAt?: number; refuseAt?: number; cutAt?: number }): typeof fetch` (answers `/v1/messages` with a real server-sent-event body) and `scriptFor(seed: WorldSeed, unit: UnitId): ScriptedTurn[]` (the expected run).
Behaviour: events in order: `unit` running, then `field` and `reading` (Reader) or per turn `call`, `result`, `note` (how `progress` for `between_tools` thinking blocks, `summary` for summarised thinking, `text` for text blocks) and `words` (the reason inside the final tool's streamed input; deltas pushed about every 250 ms; at most 1,200 characters of model text a turn), then `verdict` (from `engine.check`) or `proposal` (from `engine.propose`), then `unit` done with model, time to first event, time, cost, tokens and request ids. Before each turn `budget.reserve(estimateMicros)` and `lanes.admit` (a focus unit waits up to 4 s, an ahead unit does not wait); after it `settle`, or `cut` with the usage known. One retry on a network error, a 5xx or a 529, only when nothing was emitted yet. A turn that ends without a tool call gets the core's reminder once. A refused final tool call is answered with the check's `why` as an error tool result, in one user message with the other results. When no live agent can decide, code does: `engine.read(id, null)`, `engine.check(id, null)`, `engine.propose(id, null)`, with `decided_by: "code"` and one of the fixed sentences of design §4.7; a stop after something was shown emits `stopped`. Assistant content is sent back unchanged.
Tests first: the Checker port returns the core's own objects; each local Payer tool's answer, a made-up option and a stray amount refused, the fallback; the Reader's happy path and a wrong reading replaced by code; the Checker's order of events; a refused `decide` then a corrected one; no tool call, the reminder, then code; a refused budget gives code with its sentence; an ahead unit is not started on a busy lane; a first-event timeout, one retry, then code; a refusal gives `stopped` with "Claude declined to answer"; the history is append-only.
Checks: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, the three test files.
Out of scope: HTTP, leases, recorded replays, the Sourcing agent.

title: Tables in use, hello, world, re-seed, state, proof of work, cleanup by alarm
spec:
Goal: a visitor gets a world of their own, and worlds clean themselves up.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §4.3 to §4.5, §6.3, §12.6.
Files: `src/jury/desk/store.ts` (helpers), `world.ts`, `src/jury/guard/pow.ts`, `precheck.ts`; `test/jury-desk-world.test.ts`, `test/jury-pow.test.ts`.
Interfaces:
`pow.ts`: `powChallenge(secret: string, bits: number, seed: string, nowMs: number): Promise<PowChallenge>`; `powCheck(secret: string, p: PowChallenge & { nonce: string }, seed: string, nowMs: number): Promise<"ok" | "expired" | "mac" | "work">`; `powWorkOk(challenge: string, nonce: string, bits: number): boolean` (the SHA-256 of `challenge:nonce` starts with `bits` zero bits; uses `sha256HexSync` of `worker/src/worldChain.ts`).
`precheck.ts`: `juryPrecheck(req: Request): Promise<{ ok: true; body: Record<string, unknown> } | { ok: false; status: number; error: string }>` (method, same origin and not cross-site, at most 16 KB read within 5 s, a JSON object, a token of the right shape when present, and for `/world` `powWorkOk`).
`store.ts`: `newWorld(ctx, a: { seed: string; pool: Pool; mode: "live" | "recorded"; netkey: string; internal: boolean; pow: string }): { row: WorldRow; token: string }`; `worldByToken(ctx, token: unknown): Promise<WorldRow | null>`; `worldByPow(ctx, challenge: string): WorldRow | null`; `dropWorld(ctx, id: string): void`; `expireWorlds(ctx, nowMs: number): number` (batches of 50); `purgeOld(ctx, nowMs: number): void`; `nextAlarm(ctx): number | null`; `chainAppend(ctx, worldId: string, kind: ChainKind, data: ChainData): void` (`nextRow` of `worker/src/worldChain.ts`, in the same synchronous stretch as the write it records); `chainOf(ctx, worldId: string): ChainView`; `keyed(ctx, value: string): Promise<string>` (HMAC with the day's secret, which is made on first use, changes every UTC day and is deleted after 48 hours).
Handlers: `hello` (a seed: the first 24 worlds of a UTC day walk a fixed shuffled order, then random; the company and the first invoice from `buildWorld`; the challenge with 12 bits; zero counters until the counters task); `world` (checks the challenge: HMAC, expiry, once only, and remembers it on the world so a retry returns the same world; mode "live" when config `live` is "on", else "recorded"; ingests both documents through the engine; chain row `world_opened`; passkey creation options as `newWorld` of `worker/src/trySign.ts` builds them; arms the alarm); `reseed` (a company; only before `check:catch` has started; at most 3); `state`.
Rules: the token is 32 random bytes in base64url, stored only as its SHA-256; a world lives 60 minutes, or 15 without a request (`seen` is kept in memory and written at most once a minute); requests purge nothing; no address is stored anywhere, only `keyed(networkKey(ip))`.
Tests first: hello then world with a solved proof of work; a wrong, expired and reused challenge; a retried `world` returns the same world; the re-seed rules; `state` returns `last_seq`; with a fake clock an instance with no traffic has no world row 61 minutes after the last world opened, and no request deletes anything; the test's address appears in no row of any table; the token is stored hashed; every refusal of the precheck.
Checks: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, the two test files.
Out of scope: units and streams, signing, pools and the queue (task admission), the real caps.

title: The event log, the stream and long-poll endpoints, the unit runner
spec:
Goal: a visitor watches an agent work while the real call is in flight, and can reconnect at any point.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §4.6, §4.7; docs/jury-demo/spike.md for what a disconnect does.
Files: `src/jury/desk/units.ts`, `src/jury/desk/store.ts` (event and unit helpers); `test/jury-desk-units.test.ts`, `test/jury-stream.test.ts`.
Interfaces: `emitEvent(ctx, worldId: string, e: JuryEventInput): JuryEvent` (appends to `jr_events` with the next sequence number and pushes to the world's open stream); `pushDelta(ctx, worldId: string, d: JuryDelta): void` (live only; the text so far of an open block is kept in memory for a viewer that reconnects); `UNIT_ORDER: { two: UnitId[]; one: UnitId[] }`; `startUnit(ctx, world: WorldRow, unit: UnitId, priority: "focus" | "ahead"): "started" | "running" | "done" | "not_yet"`; `reconcileUnits(ctx, nowMs: number): Promise<void>`; `registerUnit(unit: UnitId | "talk", run: (ctx, world, unit) => Promise<RunOutcome>): void` (so a later task adds the Sourcing and talk units without editing the runner).
Handlers: `stream` (`text/event-stream` with `cache-control: no-store`: the stored events after `after`, then live ones; `id`, `event`, `data` frames through `sseFrame`; deltas carry no id; one stream per world, a new one closes the old; at most 60 s; a comment line every 15 s; over 400 open streams answer `200 {poll: true}`; `run` starts that unit when it is the world's next one, `ahead` one more at low priority) and `events` (a long poll that returns as soon as an event after `after` exists or after `wait_ms`, at most 8,000: `{events, next, running}`).
Runner: the lease (`jr_units`, 30 s, extended per turn) is taken with no `await` before it; at most two live attempts; the run promise is handed to `ctx.keepAlive`; when a unit ends: a chain row `agent_step` with `{unit, source, outcome}` and one `jr_calls` row. A world in recorded mode asks `ctx.opts.recorded` for a replay through a hook `replay?: (ctx, world, unit) => Promise<boolean>` set by the recorder task; until then code decides at once. `reconcileUnits`: a unit whose lease has run out is marked failed and code decides for it.
Tests first (the local relay with `standInAnthropic`): events arrive in at least three chunks spread over time; a resume after N returns exactly the later events; a second stream closes the first; a viewer that aborts mid-turn: the turn still ends, writes its verdict, frees its lease and settles its reservation; a slow reader does not delay the upstream (fake clock); the long poll returns on the first new event; a unit asked out of order answers `not_yet`; a unit asked twice runs once; a lease that runs out is closed by the alarm and code decides; one Checker unit writes at most 40 rows.
Checks: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, the two test files.
Out of scope: the Sourcing and talk units; the replay itself; admission.

title: Passkey, test signer, sign, the one pay endpoint with its state machine
spec:
Goal: a real signature over the exact terms, and one endpoint that pays the signed terms once and refuses anything else for a real reason.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §8.2 to §8.6.
Files: `src/jury/desk/sign.ts`, `pay.ts`, `src/jury/rails/chain.ts`; `test/jury-sign.test.ts`, `test/jury-pay.test.ts`.
Interfaces: `chain.ts`: `type PayState = "none" | "paying" | "created" | "sent" | "paid" | "simulated" | "held"`; `payRow(ctx, worldId: string): PayRowData | null`; `setPay(ctx, worldId: string, patch: Partial<PayRowData>): void` (written before the `await` that follows). `pay.ts`: `payOnce(ctx, world: WorldRow, proposalId: string, canonical: string, requestId: string): Promise<PayAnswer>`; `resumePayments(ctx, nowMs: number): Promise<void>` (a no-op until task rails-wire).
Handlers: `passkey` (create: `verifyRegistration` of `worker/src/trySign.ts` against the world's one-time challenge, nulled before the await; reuse: stores `{id, x, y}` as unproven, proven by the first valid assertion); `signer` (the test key's public point, checked to be on the curve); `sign` (`engine.approve`; accepts only the stored proposal's terms; success: a chain row `signature` whose data is exactly `{proposal_id, terms_sha256}`, a `sign` event, `ctx.count("signatures_passkey" | "signatures_test")`; a refusal is `200 {verified: false, why, reason, terms_sha256, signed_sha256}` with a chain row `refusal`; only unexpected failures (an unknown credential, a wrong origin) count, and at 5 the world closes); `pay` (`payOnce`); `decide` (`decline` or `overrule`, recorded in the world's state).
`payOnce`: `engine.execute` with a rail that wraps `ctx.rails.pay` and the state machine of §8.5: `paying` fixes the request id; a second call while a chain runs waits for the outcome; emits a `rail` event per answer; chain row `execution` with `{proposal_id, execution_id, terms_sha256, source}`; after it `auditExecutions` and `ctx.count("past_limit_unsigned", violations)`. A refusal: chain row `refusal`, a `refusal` event, `rail_calls: 0`, `verify_ms` measured around the verification, `changed` from the engine. These refusals are counted only in the world's own tamper count: the 21st answers 429 with "That is a lot of attempts for one test world. Open another to go on." They never lock an address.
The rail-client path is not reachable from the refusal branch: `payOnce` gets the rail only after the verification has passed.
Tests first: passkey create, reuse, proven on the first assertion; another world's credential refused; a replayed assertion; the test signer; `sign` with other terms is refused; `pay` before `sign` answers `not_signed`; the signed terms pay once; 20 parallel `pay` calls reach `ctx.rails.pay` once; one cent, another IBAN and both: `verified: false`, `rail_calls: 0`, the rail not called, a chain refusal row; edited back: `already_paid`; the 21st changed-terms attempt; `decide`'s rules; a jury passkey opens nothing on the relay or on `/try/sign` (in the manner of `test/try-sign-separation.test.ts`).
Checks: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, the two test files.
Out of scope: the real Airwallex client (tasks rails-awx and rails-wire); books.

title: The page, its script's build, the reducer, the components, screens 0 and 1
spec:
Goal: the page's frame and the first two screens, driven by the event log.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §3, §4.2, §4.6.
Files: `src/jury/page/page.ts`, `css.ts`, `build.ts`; `src/jury/client/main.ts`, `api.ts`, `stream.ts`, `reduce.ts`, `ui.ts`, `pow.ts`, `screens/s0.ts`, `screens/s1.ts`; `src/jury/shared/canonical.ts`, `sha256.ts`, `money.ts`; `src/jury/copy.ts` (s0, s1, the states); `test/jury-build.test.ts`, `test/jury-copy.test.ts`, `test/jury-reduce.test.ts`.
Interfaces: `build.ts`: `juryClientScript(): string` (orders the files of `src/jury/client/` and `src/jury/shared/` by their imports, transpiles each with `ts.transpileModule`, removes `import` lines and `export` keywords, joins them in one function). `page.ts`: `juryPage(): string` through `page({ title, description, tab: "try", css, body, data, js, source, real })` of `src/redesign/ui.ts`. `reduce.ts` (pure): `interface View { screen: number; world: WorldView | null; units: Record<string, UnitState>; trips: Trip[]; reading: Partial<Record<Role, ApReading>>; verdicts: Partial<Record<Role, VerdictD>>; proposal: ProposalD | null; paid: PaidView | null; mode: "stream" | "poll" }`, `reduce(v: View, e: JuryEvent | JuryDelta): View`. `stream.ts`: `openStream(o: { token: string; after: number; run?: UnitId; ahead?: UnitId; on(e: JuryEvent | JuryDelta): void; onMode(m: "stream" | "poll"): void }): { close(): void }` (reads `response.body` with a `TextDecoder` and `sseParser`; if no byte arrives within 2 s while a unit runs, aborts and long-polls `events` for the rest of the visit; reconnects on `visibilitychange` and `online` with the last sequence number). `api.ts`: `call<T>(path: string, body: unknown): Promise<{ data: T; ms: number }>` (measures the round trip with `performance.now()`; retries a network error, 502, 503 and 504 three times with back-off, sending the same body). `pow.ts`: `solve(p: PowChallenge, slice?: number): Promise<string>` (synchronous SHA-256 in short slices).
Components (`ui.ts`): the band "Test money · Airwallex sandbox · Metal testnet" with the "What's real?" fold; the progress row of nine steps; the live line (who, model, live or recorded, a running clock; rows "→ label ← the first sentence of the tool's answer"; the agent's words marked "its own words, not checked yet"; three rows high, older rows fold into "{n} checks"); the pill; the invoice paper with chips; the round-trips list (a fold on a phone; from 1024 px the right column with the invoice, a stamp per finished step and the list); folds. Use the tokens and components of `src/redesign/ui.ts` (`.card`, `.btn.primary.big`, `.pill`, `.st-bubble`, `.dots`) and `MOTION` and `STAGE` of `src/try/sign.ts`; no new colour, font or animation.
Screens 0 and 1 as design §3: the company pick and re-seed, the queue line, the recorded badge, "ran live {n} s ago, while you read", the three lines from code, "Decline and continue". Tool names map to labels in the copy (supplier on file?, bank details?, history?, totals?, limits?, contract or order?).
Rules: only named imports and exports; imports only from the two folders; no timer outside `stream.ts`, `api.ts` and `pow.ts`; everything is rendered with `textContent`; the token lives in `sessionStorage`; the fragment keys (`#j=`, `#e=`) are read, removed from the address bar and sent; the site's tabs are hidden while a world runs; nothing is drawn before its response; focus moves to the heading on a screen change; the live area has `aria-live="off"` and one polite message per finished event; reduced motion appends whole sentences.
Word budgets: screen 0 at most 30 words, every other screen at most 45, outside the live area and the invoice; exactly one `.btn.primary.big` per screen.
Tests first: the built script has no `import` or `export`, no top-level name twice, and `new Function(code)` parses it; the copy's words per screen are within budget and hold none of: stand-in, certified, endorsed, raw reasoning, people, Face ID signatures, money moved without a signature; the reducer turns a Checker run's events into the expected view and a replay of the same log gives the same view; `canonical` equals the Worker's on 100 generated term objects; the page's SHA-256 equals `sha256HexSync`.
Checks: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, the three test files, `npm run relay:pages && (cd worker && npx tsc --noEmit)`.
Out of scope: screens 2 to 8; passkey code.

title: Screens 2 to 4: sign, paid, change it yourself; a minimal end card
spec:
Goal: the visitor signs on their own device, sees the payment arrive row by row, then edits the terms and is refused with the evidence. This completes the thin slice.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §3 (screens 2 to 4), §8.2 to §8.6.
Files: `src/jury/client/passkey.ts`, `screens/s2.ts`, `s3.ts`, `s4.ts`, `s8.ts` (minimal: heading, ids, the replay link); `src/jury/copy.ts` (s2 to s4); `src/try/verify.ts` (one additive change); `test/try-verify.test.ts` (added cases), `test/jury-copy.test.ts` (extended), `test/jury-amount.test.ts`.
Interfaces (`passkey.ts`): `method(): string` ("Face ID", "Touch ID", "fingerprint", "Windows Hello", else "your passkey", from the platform); `platformOk(): Promise<boolean>` (`PublicKeyCredential.isUserVerifyingPlatformAuthenticatorAvailable()`); `createPasskey(options: unknown): Promise<unknown>`; `signTerms(termsSha256Hex: string, credentialId: string): Promise<unknown>`; `testSigner(): Promise<{ publicKey: { x: string; y: string }; sign(bytes: Uint8Array): Promise<string> }>` (WebCrypto ECDSA P-256, not extractable); `remembered(): { id: string; x: string; y: string } | null` and `remember(...)` (`localStorage` key `purser.jury.passkey`). `parseAmount(input: string): string | null` in `src/jury/shared/money.ts` ("1850,01" and "1.850,01" and "1,850.01" give "1850.01"; letters give null).
Screen 2: one line "Read, checked and proposed by three Claude agents" (a fold); the Payer's live line while it works; then the amount once, the payee, the account ending, one short hash, the fold "Show the exact terms"; the sentence "This saves a test passkey on your device; you can delete it afterwards. Your device asks twice: first to create it, then to sign."; the one button in two labelled stages: "Create your CFO passkey", then "Sign {amount} with {method}", with the hint "Face ID, fingerprint or PIN: whatever your device asks". When `platformOk()` is false the button reads "Sign with the test signer", with the line "No Face ID or fingerprint on this device. A test key made in this page signs; the server checks it the same way." and the text link "Use a security key or your phone instead". A remembered passkey is offered to the new world (one prompt). When the Checker held or rejected the invoice: its reason, the button "Look at the payment anyway" and the text link "Decline it".
Screen 3: right after `sign` succeeds the page calls `pay` with the unchanged canonical terms; the heading "Signed. Paying…" becomes the outcome's headline only when the answer is back; one row per `rail` event; "Test money. Airwallex sandbox calls: {n}."; the two measured times; a fold with ids and Purser's raw answers; "Download your receipt" (`receipt.json` in the format `purser.try-sign-receipt/v1` as `/try/sign` builds it, or `purser.jury-test-receipt/v1` for the test signer) and "Check it yourself".
Screen 4: two fields prefilled with the signed amount (`inputmode="decimal"`, 16 px or larger) and IBAN; the chips "+ 1 cent" and "Other IBAN" fill a field and send nothing; the button "Pay this with my signature" is off, with the hint "Change the amount or the IBAN.", until a field differs. After the answer and not before: the stamp "Refused by Purser"; "Signed {hash} · Sent {hash}" with the differing characters marked; "Round trip {ms} ms · Airwallex calls for this attempt: 0" (the milliseconds from `api.ts`, the zero from the answer's `rail_calls`); the verdict line from `changed` ("One cent changed. The signature is worthless." for an amount, "You changed the IBAN. The signature is worthless." for an account); the text links "Raw response" and "Check it in your browser" (a passkey: `/try/verify#receipt=<base64url>&terms=<base64url>`; the test signer: six lines of WebCrypto with the values filled in). Then the button becomes "See the books". No timer delays any of this.
`src/try/verify.ts`: the fragment may also carry `&terms=<base64url of canonical terms>`; the page then checks the receipt with those terms in place of its own and adds one line "These are the terms you changed. The signature is the one you made." Pinned strings and existing behaviour stay untouched.
Tests first: on the verify page a receipt with changed terms shows "Invalid: the challenge check fails", and without `terms` everything is as before; a jury receipt renders with no "undefined"; the copy's budgets (45 words each); `parseAmount`.
Checks: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, the three test files, `npx tsx test/browser/trysign.check.ts` still green.
Out of scope: screens 5 to 7; the full summary.

title: The Airwallex client for the demo: table, call ledger, payout chain, card decline
spec:
Goal: real sandbox calls behind an allowlist and a ledger that is checked before each request, with a labelled simulated fallback for every failure.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §9.1 to §9.6; the fixtures in `test/fixtures/jury-awx/`.
Files: `src/jury/rails/awx.ts`, `ledger.ts`, `labels.ts`; `src/airwallex/transferBody.ts` (move the body of `createPayoutTransfer` out of `src/airwallex/adapter.ts` as `payoutTransferBody(t: NewPayoutTransfer): Record<string, unknown>`; the adapter calls it); `worker/src/juryRails.ts` (`awxRails`); `test/support/jurySandboxFake.ts`; `test/jury-rails-pin.test.ts`, `test/jury-awx.test.ts`, `test/jury-rail-labels.test.ts`.
Interfaces:
`awx.ts`: `JURY_AWX_HOST = "api.sandbox.airwallex.com"`; `JURY_AWX_ALLOWED: readonly { method: "GET" | "POST"; path: RegExp; onBehalfOf: "required" | "never"; query: null | "request_id" }[]` (exactly: login never; `transfers/create` required; `simulation/transfers/<uuid>/transition` required; `GET transfers` with `request_id` required; `simulation/issuing/create` never); `class JuryAwxNotAllowed extends Error`; `juryAwxUrl(method: string, url: string, onBehalfOf: string | null): URL` (throws unless the table has it: host, HTTPS, no userinfo, no other query); `type AwxAnswer = { ok: true; status: number; json: Record<string, unknown>; ms: number } | { ok: false; why: "timeout" | "http" | "lost"; status: number; code: string | null; ms: number }`; `class JuryAwx { constructor(cfg: { clientId: string; secret: string; account: string; fetch?: typeof fetch; now?: () => number }); createTransfer(body: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<AwxAnswer>; transition(id: string, to: "SENT" | "PAID"): Promise<AwxAnswer>; findTransfer(requestId: string): Promise<AwxAnswer>; cardCharge(a: { cardId: string; amount: string; merchant: string; mcc: string }): Promise<AwxAnswer> }` (one login at a time, the token kept in memory until a minute before it expires, 8 s per call, a `POST` is never sent twice).
`ledger.ts`: `interface RailCaps { perWorld: number; perDay: Record<Pool, number> }`; `railReserve(sql: Sql, a: { world: string; pool: Pool; rail: "airwallex" | "metal"; n: number; day: string }, caps: RailCaps): boolean`; `railCall(sql, a: { world: string; pool: Pool; rail: "airwallex" | "metal"; op: string; requestId: string | null; day: string }): number` (writes the row before the request; throws past the visitor's cap); `railDone(sql, id: number, status: string, http: number, ms: number): void`; `railRelease(sql, world: string, rail: "airwallex" | "metal", n: number, day: string): void`; `railCount(sql, world: string, rail: "airwallex" | "metal"): number`.
`labels.ts`: `type PayOutcome = "paid" | "created" | "in_approval" | "refused" | "not_sent" | "lost"`; `payLabel(o: PayOutcome, d: { id?: string; status?: string; code?: string; reason?: string }, records: SandboxFacts["records"]): { headline: PaidView["headline"]; label: string; real: { href: string; label: string } }`; `cardLabel(...)` and `mandateLabel(...)` likewise, with exactly the sentences of design §9.6.
`awxRails(sql: Sql, cfg: { clientId: string; secret: string; fetch?: typeof fetch }, sandbox: SandboxFacts, conf: (key: string) => string | null, now: () => Date): Pick<Rails, "pay" | "decline">`.
Behaviour of `pay`: reserve 4 (3 and the lookup spare) or return the simulated outcome; the gate (8 chains in flight, at most 8 s of waiting, then simulated with "many visitors at once"); the breaker (three failures in a row close the lane for 60 s); the balance guard (config `rail_balance_cents` below 500000 gives "the sandbox test account needs a top-up") and its decrement by amount plus fee; create with the product's body, `transfer_method: "LOCAL"`, the reference being the invoice number, `metadata: {approval_sha256, purser_demo: "1"}`; then SENT and PAID; a lost create answer is looked up by request id before anything else; `IN_APPROVAL` sets config `rails_awx` to "tripped"; a `rail` event per answered call; logins are counted in the day's ledger with an empty world. title: The Sourcing agent's unit, the talk step, the retry and the signed raise
spec:
Goal: the agent tries to overspend on its own card and mandate, the rails answer, the visitor may talk to it, and only a signature raises the limit.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §3 (screens 6 and 7), §7.5, §9.1, §9.3.
Files: `src/jury/desk/overspend.ts`, `src/jury/agents/run.ts` (add `runSourcing`); `test/jury-overspend.test.ts`.
Interface: `runSourcing(unit: UnitId, world: WorldRow, facts: WorldFacts, port: SourcingPort, rails: Rails, talk: null | { text: string }, d: RunDeps): Promise<RunOutcome>`; register it for `sourcing` and `talk` with `registerUnit` of `src/jury/desk/units.ts`.
Behaviour of `sourcing`: the agent's `pay_by_card` makes code call `ctx.rails.decline` (attempt 1) with the scenario's amount and merchant; the result text is "Airwallex sandbox: DECLINED, LIMIT_EXCEEDED (limit {limit} EUR)." or the simulated sentence. `pay_under_mandate` makes code call `ctx.rails.mandate`; the result text is the state read and code's comparison: "{amount} is over the mandate's cap of {cap}; Metal would refuse it." Then `read_decline`, `propose_raise` or `no_raise` through `answerDeclineTool`. If the agent ends without trying a rail, code makes the attempt and the row is marked "tried by code". Each rail answer is also a `rail` event.
`talk {token, n, text}`: at most 280 characters after `cleanText` (`src/ap/reading.ts`) removes control and invisible characters; three a world; refused with "The live agents are off right now." when no live call is possible. A fresh short conversation: the system prompt, the situation in code's words, the fixed talk line, then the visitor's words as a user turn of their own; never inside a tool result. If the agent calls `pay_by_card` again: a second real decline when the visitor's fifth call is free and no raise was signed, else the simulated rule with its label. The text is not stored, not logged and not written to the chain; the chain row says only what the agent did and what the rail answered. A `refusal` stop is shown as "Claude declined to answer this message."
`attempt {token}`: the same second attempt, started by the visitor ("Send its request to the card anyway").
`raise {token}`: `engine.proposePolicy({key: "card.sourcing.per_tx", to, reason})` with `to` from the agent's accepted proposal or `declineFallback`; the page signs it with `sign`; then a `policy` event and a `rail` event with rail "purser", source "simulated" and status "approved in your test world". No request goes to Airwallex after a raise, ever.
Tests first: the happy path's events; an agent that never tries, then code tries; a talk that makes it try again gives a second decline on the fake and never a third; after a raise no rail request at all; no model input can change the amount; control characters cleaned, 281 characters refused, a fourth talk refused; the typed text is in no table and no log line (spy on `console`); a refusal; live off.

title: Screen 8: the summary, the folds, every state's sentence
spec:
Goal: the end card that says what happened, honestly, and lets the visitor verify, replay and export.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §3 (screen 8 and the corners), §11, §14.
Files: `src/jury/client/screens/s8.ts` (full), `src/jury/copy.ts` (s8 and every state: queued, recorded, a stopped attempt, expired, connection lost, passkey cancelled, paused), `src/jury/page/page.ts` (the static "paused" card; the prompts in the page's data); `test/jury-copy.test.ts` (extended), `test/jury-prompts.test.ts`.
Screen: the heading "That's Purser."; one line of what the visitor did; per invoice the graded line from `end`; the counter line "{played} scenarios played · {frauds_stopped} frauds stopped · {signatures_passkey} signatures with a passkey · 0 payments past a limit without a signature · since {date}" (the zero is the answer's number) with the frauds' split and today's live share one tap away; the site's tabs return. Folds: "The agents as a team" (per agent the model and effort, live, recorded or code, what it did, time, cost, the visit's total; for the Checker the note "in the product this agent runs on Claude Opus 5.5"); "Ids and verify" (the world, the seed, the proposal, the terms hash, the transfer or simulated id, the authorization id, the block number, the chain's head, "Verify the chain" recomputed in the browser); "What is fixed, what is live" ("Fixed: this scenario's documents and the order of the steps. Live: every agent decision, every signature check, every rail answer.", then each agent's system prompt and tool definitions word for word and which core it runs, and that the Sourcing agent's two purchase tools are this demo's and that it is told to make the purchase); "More" ("Replay this scenario: the same documents; the agents decide again, their words will differ", "Another scenario", "Your test company as an export" as a JSON download from `export`, "The Purser Cloud demo: a separate demo world with seeded test companies, not the one you just used" when a URL is set, one line of What's next, and "Visa is not part of this hands-on demo: a Visa Intelligent Commerce purchase through Airwallex's Airi needs the cardholder's own tap. The paid run of 7 November" with the link `/runs#vic-1`). "Try live again" when the world was recorded. The one button: "See the real runs".
The static card, when `hello` cannot be reached or the demo is paused: "The live demo is paused. Watch the recorded run" with the video link and the real runs.
Rules: at most 45 words outside the folds; one main button; the prompts shown are built at build time from the cores' own constants.
Tests first: the copy's budgets and forbidden phrasings (no "people", no "Face ID signatures", no "money moved without a signature", no "stand-in"); the prompts in the page equal `CHECKER_SYSTEM`, the Payer's and the Sourcing agent's; every state has a sentence and, where it applies, a button.
Checks: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, the two test files, `npm run relay:pages && (cd worker && npx tsc --noEmit)`.
Out of scope: `/go/count`.

title: The 24 scenarios and the sweep that proves them
spec:
Goal: at least 24 tested scenarios whose code floors are computed by the product's code, not typed in.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §6.2, §6.3 (the table is the specification).
Files: `src/jury/scenario/library.ts` (all 24), additions to `blocks.ts`, `docs.ts`, `world.ts`; `test/jury-library.test.ts`.
Interface additions: `orderOfDay(day: string): number[]` (a fixed shuffle of 0..23 per UTC day); `FLOOR_BY_LIMIT: readonly string[]` (the ids of the scenarios whose floor is `ask_cfo` by the limit).
Rules: every row of the table of §6.2: company, event, language, currency, kind, the sign invoice's language and kind, the expected answers with their accepted set and a one-sentence `because`. Every catch invoice that is not legit is above the company's limit or in another currency. `demo-day` is S01 with n = 0.
The floors are what the test computes: for 200 seeds per scenario, after the parser's own reading, `codeRequires(engine.checkerCase(id), codeFindings(engine.checkerCase(id)))` must give the table's floor and one of its codes (`possible_fraud`, `duplicate`, `possible_duplicate`, `iban_invalid`, `new_supplier`, `credit_note`, or the limit's rule `above_alone_limit` or `alone_limit_other_currency`). If a document does not produce its floor, change the document. If the product's code truly has no such rule, set `floor` to what code computes, add the id to `FLOOR_BY_LIMIT`, and say so in the task's report: never add a check to the demo.
Tests first: the sweep above; both documents parse and the parser's reading passes `readingCheck`; the sign invoice's floor is `ask_cfo` by `above_alone_limit`; every IBAN passes `ibanValid`; every sign supplier key is one of `SIGN_SUPPLIERS`; the expected answer is never looser than the floor; the coverage counts of §6.2; English, Dutch and German, and EUR, USD and GBP are all present; `orderOfDay` is a permutation.
Checks: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, the test file.
Out of scope: recordings, evals.

title: Recorded real runs: the format, the recorder, the replay
spec:
Goal: a recorded real run of every agent on every scenario, replayed at its own pace and labelled, that never decides for a visitor.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §4.7, §7.4.
Files: `src/cli/juryRecord.ts`, `src/jury/agents/recorded.ts`, the replay hook in `src/jury/desk/units.ts`, the recorded seed in `src/jury/desk/world.ts`; `docs/demo/jury-recorded.json` (written by the run); `test/jury-recorded.test.ts`.
Interfaces: `RECORDED_FORMAT = "kit11.jury-recorded/v2"`; `interface RecordedUnit { model: string | null; attempt: number; completed: boolean; outcome: string | null; events: { after_ms: number; e: JuryEventInput }[] }`; `interface RecordedLibrary { format: typeof RECORDED_FORMAT; recorded_on: string; scenarios: Record<string, { seed: string; units: Partial<Record<UnitId, RecordedUnit>>; talks: Record<string, RecordedUnit> }> }`; `readRecorded(raw: unknown): RecordedLibrary | null`; `recordedSeed(lib: RecordedLibrary, scenarioId: string): string | null`; `replayRecorded(ctx: DeskCtx, world: WorldRow, unit: UnitId, lib: RecordedLibrary, wait: (ms: number) => Promise<void>): Promise<boolean>` (emits each event after its delay clamped to 400 to 2,500 ms, with `source: "recorded"` and the label "recorded {date}: a real run of this agent on this scenario" on the first `unit` event; returns false when the library has no such unit).
`npm run jury:record -- --all | --scenario S01` runs the real desk in this process against the live API (`KIT11_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, long timeouts, simulated rails), once per scenario, with the settings that will ship; it keeps the first complete run, right or wrong, with its attempt number; an incomplete run is recorded as incomplete and the scenario is listed. It needs `JURY_RECORD_GO=yes`, prints its expected spend first (about USD 2.50) and must not be run during judging hours or the Demo Day evening. It also records one exchange per talk chip per scenario.
Rules: a recording never decides: after a replay the world's decision is code's (`decided_by: "code"`); its text is never edited; a world that opens in recorded mode gets `recordedSeed`, so the recording's figures are the invoice's; a recorded run adds USD 0 to the visit's cost and its clock says "recorded timing". The file holds no token, signature or key and stays under 300 KB.
Tests first: `readRecorded` refuses other formats; the pacing with a fake clock (both clamps); every replayed `unit` event is marked recorded and labelled before the first other event; the decision after a replay is code's; the file's size and a scan for `sk-`, `authorization` and `"token"`; the talk chips replay; a world in recorded mode has the recorded seed.
Checks: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, the test file; gitleaks locally on the recording before committing.
Out of scope: evals.

title: The eval that picks the models, and the measured cost of a visit
spec:
Goal: the cheapest model that passes for each agent, and the real cost per visit, before the caps are set.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §7.6, §7.7.
Files: `src/cli/juryEvals.ts`, `docs/evals/jury.json` (written), `docs/agent-evals.md` (a table added), `src/jury/agents/settings.ts` (the defaults, once measured); `test/jury-evals-rule.test.ts`.
Interfaces: `interface EvalRow { agent: AgentId; config: string; settings: AgentSettings; runs: number; pass: number; safe: boolean; failures: { scenario: string; got: string; expected: string }[]; ttfeP95: number; totalP95: number; costMicros: number }`; `interface EvalReport { ran_on: string; rows: EvalRow[]; visit: null | { costMicros: number; perAgent: Record<AgentId, { ttfeP50: number; ttfeP95: number; totalP50: number; totalP95: number; costMicros: number }> } }`; `THRESHOLDS = { reader: 0.98, checker: 0.90, payer: 0.95 }`; `pickModels(report: EvalReport): Record<AgentId, AgentSettings>` (pure: the cheapest configuration that passes its threshold, is safe and meets the time targets; if none, the product's configuration and a warning).
`npm run jury:evals -- --runs 2` runs one seed per scenario per configuration: Reader on Haiku 5.5; Checker on Haiku 5.5 (summarised thinking, effort low and medium), on Sonnet 5.5 (`between_tools` at medium, and summarised at low) and once on the product's configuration (`CHECKER_MODEL`, `CHECKER_EFFORT`, `CHECKER_MAX_TURNS`) as the baseline row; Payer on Haiku 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5. A Checker run passes when the agent's own action is in the scenario's accepted set; `safe` is true only when, after `enforce`, no catch invoice that is not legit is paid in any run. `--visit` then runs three whole visits (S01, S07, S16) through the desk with the chosen settings and prints the measured cost per visit and the times per agent. The command needs `JURY_EVALS_GO=yes`, prints its expected spend first (about USD 5) and must not run during judging hours.
The report states the failures per scenario and that the eval set is the demo's own 24 scenarios. After the run: set `DEFAULT_SETTINGS` to the choice and write the measured cost per visit and the proposed caps into `docs/jury-demo/spike.md`.
Tests first: `pickModels` on made-up reports (Haiku passes: Haiku; only Sonnet passes: Sonnet; nothing passes: the product's configuration with a warning; an unsafe configuration is never chosen); the thresholds.
Checks: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, the test file.
Out of scope: the admin view's model switch.

title: The dollar caps ledger and the lanes that follow the provider's headers
spec:
Goal: hard dollar caps that cannot be passed or emptied without spend, and gates that follow Anthropic's own limits.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §12.1, §12.3, §12.4.
Files: `src/jury/guard/config.ts`, `budget.ts`, `lanes.ts`, `defaults.ts` (the default ports become the real ones); `test/jury-budget.test.ts`, `test/jury-lanes.test.ts`.
Interfaces:
`config.ts`: `CONFIG_DEFAULTS: Record<string, string>` (every switch off and every cap 0 until set); `CEILINGS: Record<string, number>` (per world USD 0.50; a pool's day USD 40; all-time USD 78; Airwallex calls a day 1,500; Metal calls a day 1,000); `conf(sql: Sql, key: string): string`; `setConf(sql: Sql, key: string, value: string, nowMs: number): { ok: true } | { ok: false; why: string }` (refuses past a ceiling and any model `callCostMicros` cannot price; writes a `jr_admin_log` row with the old and the new value).
`budget.ts`: `sqlBudget(sql: Sql, now: () => Date, hasKey: () => boolean): Budget & { figures(): { all: number; today: Record<Pool, number>; reservedOpen: number; spentBefore: number } }`.
`lanes.ts`: `memoryLanes(now: () => number): Lanes & { state(): Record<Lane, { inFlight: number; closedUntil: number; limits: Record<string, number>; remaining: Record<string, number>; recent: boolean[] }> }`.
Keys: `live`, `cap_world_micros` (300000; 150000 for an event key), `cap_day_micros.<pool>`, `cap_day_overrides` (JSON by date and pool), `cap_all_micros` (76000000), `reserve_micros` (30000000) and `reserve_until` ("2026-11-20T00:00:00Z"), `spent_before_micros`.
Rules: in one synchronous stretch with no `await` before the reservation row is written: the switch and the key; then the world's, the pool's day's and the all-time room, each counted as spent plus open reservations plus this one, the all-time room reduced by the held-back reserve until its date; then the `jr_resv` row and the three `jr_spend` scopes (`all`, `day:<date>:<pool>`, `world:<id>`). `settle` books the real cost; `cut(id, known)` books the known usage, or the whole reserve when `known` is null; `reconcile` closes reservations older than 60 s as cut with null. The refusal sentences are the `BudgetWhy` values. Lanes: per model keep the last `anthropic-ratelimit-{requests,input-tokens,output-tokens}-{limit,remaining}` and `retry-after`; a lane is closed while remaining requests or tokens are under 15% of the limit, for the `retry-after` time after a 429 or 529, and for 60 s when 5 of its last 10 calls failed within two minutes; a focus unit goes before an ahead unit; an ahead unit is admitted only while more than half the lane is free; until headers have been seen the ceiling in flight is 40 for Haiku and Sonnet and 12 for Opus.
Tests first: each cap refuses with its own sentence; the order of the checks; 20 parallel reserves never pass a cap; a settle is exact to the micro-dollar; a cut call bills the known usage; `reconcile`; the held-back reserve before and after its date; the day overrides; a cap above its ceiling is refused; an unpriced model is refused; with no configuration every reserve is refused with "the live agents are switched off"; headers close and reopen a lane; a 429's `retry-after`; the breaker; the priority rule.
Checks: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, the two test files, `test/jury-desk-units.test.ts` still green.
Out of scope: admission; the admin page.

title: Pools and keys, the mode per world, the queue, limits by token, protect
spec:
Goal: a room on one Wi-Fi is never locked out, a script cannot starve the jurors, and nobody gets an error at the door.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §12.2, §12.5, §12.6.
Files: `src/jury/guard/keys.ts`, `admission.ts`, `limits.ts`; `src/jury/desk/world.ts` (use them); `test/jury-admission.test.ts`.
Interfaces:
`keys.ts`: `makeKey(secret: string, k: { pool: "juror" | "event"; id: string; from: string; to: string }): Promise<string>` (a base64url payload and an HMAC); `readKey(secret: string, key: string, nowMs: number): Promise<{ pool: Pool; id: string } | null>` (null when forged or outside its time).
`admission.ts`: `interface Admit { mode: "live" | "recorded"; pool: Pool; why: string | null; queued: null | { ticket: string; position: number; etaS: number } }`; `admit(ctx: DeskCtx, a: { addr: string; net: string; key: string | null; wait: boolean; ticket: string | null; internal: boolean }): Promise<Admit>`; `powBits(ctx: DeskCtx, net: string): number` (12 when calm; 16 when one network opens more than ten worlds a minute or everyone more than 120; 20 under protect).
`limits.ts` (in memory): `worldLimiter(now: () => number): { hit(worldId: string, kind: "req" | "tamper" | "talk" | "raise" | "reseed" | "export"): boolean }` (120 requests a minute; 20, 3, 3, 3, 3 a world).
Rules: the pool comes from the key the page read from the fragment and sent in `hello` and `world`; without a valid key the pool is public. A world is live when: config `live` is on and not `protect`; the pool's day has room for one expected visit (USD 0.08); the lanes of the models in use are open; live worlds open are under the ceiling (150); the address has opened fewer live worlds in the last ten minutes than its pool allows (public 6, juror 20, event 150). Otherwise it opens in recorded mode with the reason; a person is never answered 429. While `wait` is true and only capacity is missing, `world` answers 202 with a ticket, the position and an estimate, for at most 20 seconds; the ticket carries the used challenge so a retry needs no new proof of work. New worlds per address: 12 an hour and 40 a day (public); per network 60 an hour; past them the world is recorded. The ceiling on open worlds (3,000) is the one refusal: 503 with `retry_ms` and "The demo is full for a moment. Try again shortly." Admission counters are one row per keyed hash, kind and window in `jr_admit` (an upsert), never a row per hit. Worlds opened with the admin token in `internal` are flagged and count nowhere public. Limits inside a world use the world's token only.
Tests first: 150 worlds behind one address with an event key are all live while capacity lasts; without the key the seventh in ten minutes is recorded; a script that opens 300 public worlds leaves the juror and event pools' dollars and rail calls untouched; a forged or expired key is the public pool; the queue's order and its 20 seconds; protect; the bits rise with the rate; a second world on the same address is not slowed by the first's limits; the door's one refusal.
Checks: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, the test file, `test/jury-desk-world.test.ts` still green.
Out of scope: the admin API; the counters.

title: The public counters, health, the admin API and the admin page
spec:
Goal: the owner sees and steers everything during judging without a deploy, and nobody else can.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §11.3, §12.8.
Files: `src/jury/desk/admin.ts`, `src/jury/desk/counters.ts` (the endpoint), `src/jury/page/admin.ts`; `test/jury-admin.test.ts`.
Handlers: `counters` (`CountersAnswer`; `since` is the first world's date; internal worlds are not in it); `health` (`{state, version, cores: {checker: "product", payer: "demo" | "product", sourcing: "product and demo"}}`); `admin` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and `{op}`: `status`, `set {key, value}`, `key {pool, id, from, to}` (returns the key and the URL to print), `protect {on}`, `balance {cents}`, `warm` (answers "not built" until task pre-ramp).
Rules: the token is at least 32 random bytes; it is checked first, in constant time, against `opts.adminTokenSha256`; without that secret the endpoint answers 404; a correct token is never locked out; wrong tokens are counted for everyone together and, past 50 in ten minutes, answered 429. `status` holds, with no world id and no address: the state and why; the switches (`live`, `rails_awx`, `rails_metal`, `open`, `protect`); worlds open, today, finished, by mode; per agent the last hour's calls, live share, time to first event and total time (p50, p95) and errors by reason, from `jr_calls`; per lane the headroom and state; spend today per pool and all-time against each cap, and reserved but not billed; per rail the calls today per pool against the caps, logins, the running balance, the live and simulated share, the last error; Metal reads today; new worlds a minute by keyed-hash network (the top five, hashes cut to 8 characters); the counters; the last 20 errors; the last 20 changes; the expected live share for 50 simultaneous visitors (from the lanes' headroom and the measured tokens per visit). `set` goes through `setConf` (ceilings, priced models only).
The page (`/go/admin#k=<token>`): static; the token is read from the fragment and sent only as the Bearer header; it polls only while the tab is visible, every 5 s while an event key is active and every 20 s otherwise; switches, caps, pool shares, models, the rail balance, the key maker.
Tests first: a right, a wrong and a missing token; a flood of wrong tokens does not lock out the right one; `set` writes the log and respects the ceilings; `status` holds no world id and no address (scan it); the counters leave internal worlds out; `health` names the cores.
Checks: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, the test file, `npm run relay:pages && (cd worker && npx tsc --noEmit)`; add `/go/admin` to the page checks' list only in task site-wiring.
Out of scope: `/go/count`; the pre-ramp.

title: The CFO relay drops the demo's Airwallex webhooks
spec:
Goal: public demo traffic can never push the owner's own webhook events out of the relay or wake his agents.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §9.9; `worker/src/core.ts` `Relay.hook` (it keeps 500 events and drops the oldest).
Files: `worker/src/core.ts` (the relay's options gain `dropHooks?: readonly string[]`; in `hook`, after the signature and the timestamp have been verified and the body parsed, an event whose raw text contains one of those strings is answered `200 {received: true}` and not stored), `worker/src/index.ts` (pass `PAGES.jurySandbox?.drop_hooks`), `src/relay/local.ts` (the same option for the tests); `test/jury-relay-filter.test.ts`.
Tests first: a correctly signed event that names the demo card's id is answered 200 and is not in the store; one whose body holds `"request_id":"jury-` is dropped; another card's event is stored as before; an unsigned or stale event is still refused with 401 whatever its body; with no sandbox file nothing is dropped; the existing webhook tests stay green.
Also check, and note in the task's report, that no runner job lists card transactions or transfers account-wide in a way that would pick up the demo's card (`declineTrigger` joins to the ledger's own cards, so an unknown card is ignored).
Checks: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, the test file and the existing relay tests, `npm run relay:pages && (cd worker && npx tsc --noEmit)`.
Out of scope: the runner; Airwallex's subscription itself.

title: npm run judge serves /go with the real desk, offline
spec:
Goal: an offline fallback that is still interactive: recorded agents, simulated rails, a real passkey on localhost.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §2 (Offline), §17.
Files: `src/cli/judge.ts` (mount the jury desk over in-memory SQLite: an adapter from the Express request to a `Request` and from the `Response` back, piping a streamed body; no model key, no rail keys, the recorded library from the bundle; add `/go` to `CHECK_PATHS`); `test/jury-judge.test.ts`.
Tests first: `npm run judge -- --check` covers `/go`; `POST /api/jury/hello` answers through the judge server; a world opens in recorded mode and its first agent card carries the recorded label; a stream is delivered in more than one chunk; no outbound request is made (the network guard of `test/support/noNetwork.ts` stays in force).
Checks: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, the test file, `npm run judge -- --check`.
Out of scope: anything that needs the network.

title: The browser checks for /go, in CI
spec:
Goal: a real browser proves the visit, the streaming, the honesty rules and the budgets.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §3, §16; model it on `test/browser/trysign.check.ts`.
Files: `test/browser/jury.check.ts` (`npx tsx test/browser/jury.check.ts [dir]`, and `--live [base]`), `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (one step in the judge job).
It serves with `startLocalRelay` built with both flags, `standInAnthropic`, the sandbox fake and the Metal fake, and drives Chromium with the virtual authenticator over CDP.
Checks it makes: one whole visit at 390 px light and one at 1440 px dark, on S01 and on S07 (a seed per scenario); on every screen at most 45 words outside the live area and the invoice (30 on screen 0) and exactly one `.btn.primary.big`; nothing wider than the screen; no console or CSP error; agent events arrive spread over time (at least three paints more than 150 ms apart); with the test server's answer to `pay` delayed by 800 ms nothing of the outcome is on screen before it; the connection dropped during the Checker, during the payout and during the passkey prompt, each recovering to the right screen; a reload on every screen returns to it; with a reduced visual viewport the send control of screen 7 stays in view; the proof of work with the CPU throttled six times is under 800 ms at the 95th percentile of 20 runs; the downloaded proof PDF holds the signed hash; the receipt verifies with `verifyReceipt`; the chain verifies; reduced motion; the recorded label is on screen before a recorded agent's first event; a device with no platform authenticator ends with the test signer and the same refusal; the page's compressed size is under 110 KB.
`--live [base]` runs two worlds against a deployed site at 390 light and 1440 dark, marked internal with the admin token from the environment, accepting live, recorded or code labels.
The whole check must stay under four minutes in CI.
Checks: the script itself, locally; `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`.
Out of scope: WebKit (task webkit-ci); the other scenarios (they run through the desk in vitest).

title: Red team of the isolation, the caps and the rails, as tests
spec:
Goal: every attack this design names is a test, and every hole it finds is fixed in the module that owns it.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §16 (Red team), §9.1, §12.
Files: `test/jury-redteam.test.ts`; fixes in the owning modules.
Cases: another world's token or credential; a world id in place of a token; a signature replayed in the same world and in another; a fresh valid signature over edited terms followed by `pay` (there is no such path: `sign` accepts only the stored terms); `pay` before `sign`; `books` and `archive` before `pay`; a raise without a signature; the talk step asking for another amount, payee or account (nothing of it reaches a request body); a body one byte too large, one key too many, a cross-site and a missing `Origin`; a talk text with control characters, of 281 characters, and a fourth attempt; a script that starts model calls and drops the connection (the caps are not emptied: cut calls are billed at what was used); spend past each cap from 20 parallel requests; stream squatting (the cap on open streams, one stream per world, the 60 seconds); 150 worlds behind one address with an event key, and without one; a flood of wrong admin tokens beside a right one; any answer, error or log line holding an upstream body, a key, a token or the RPC URL; a jury passkey opening anything on the relay or `/try/sign`; any table holding an address or the typed text after a visit; a card charge at or under the card's limit (never sent); 300 payouts from one script (the pool's day share stops it and the other pools still pay); the relay storing a demo webhook.
Each case asserts the refusal and that nothing moved, was spent or was stored.
Checks: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, the test file and every jury test.
Out of scope: load (task load-test).

title: The load test, local and on staging, and the rows budget
spec:
Goal: 50 or more people starting at the same moment get a working demo, and the numbers are known before Demo Day.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §13, §16.
Files: `src/cli/juryLoad.ts` (`npm run jury:load -- --visitors 60 --ramp 20 [--base URL] [--event-key K] [--one-address]`), `test/jury-rows.test.ts`, `docs/jury-demo/load.md`.
The script plays whole scripted visits (a software passkey; `hello`, the proof of work, `world`, the units through `stream`, `sign`, `pay`, a changed `pay`, `books`, `archive`, the Sourcing unit, one talk, `end`) and reports: requests a second, time to first event p50 and p95, the share of live worlds, 5xx count, the caps against the ledger, and per visit the rows read and written (from counters the desk keeps when `JURY_COUNT_ROWS` is set in the local harness).
Locally (in CI): 60 visitors against the local relay with `standInAnthropic` taking 1 to 4 s and the sandbox fake; it must end with no 5xx, every visitor at the summary, the caps exact to the micro-dollar and the lanes never over their ceiling.
On staging (run by the orchestrator in task go-live): 50, 150 and 300 visitors against `kit11-staging` with the local test agents and simulated rails, once from one address with an event key and once from many; the report goes into `docs/jury-demo/load.md` with the decision it supports (the ceiling on live worlds, the rail gate).
`test/jury-rows.test.ts`: one full visit, cleanup included, writes at most 450 rows; no request reads more than 60 rows (except `state`, `export` and the alarm).
Checks: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, the test file, the local run.
Out of scope: a live model or partner; tuning beyond the two ceilings.

title: The Try tab, Home, the tour, the old pages, the site tests
spec:
Goal: with the flag on, one link from the submission opens the demo directly; with it off, nothing changes.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §2 (Try tab; `/try`, `/try/sign`), §16 (gates), §18.
