title: README, claims, llms.txt, security notes, the runbook, the form text
spec:
Goal: every document says what the demo really does, in the site's vocabulary, with nothing claimed that did not run.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §14, §18.
Files: `README.md`, `llms.txt`, `docs/claims.md`, `docs/security.md`, `docs/hardening.md`, `docs/claude.md`, `docs/agent-evals.md`, `docs/judging-map.md`, the submission form text and the deck source (`src/submission/*`), `docs/jury-demo/runbook.md` (new, Dutch and English).
Content: the first-screen link and the "try it yourself" line point to `/go`; the time claim is the measured one, or absent. `docs/claims.md`: new rows for `/go`: what is live (the agents, the signature check, the changed-terms refusal); the Airwallex sandbox (which account pays: Purser's shared sandbox test account on behalf of the test company; settlement simulated at Purser's request; which card declines; at most 5 calls a visitor and 1,500 a day; what is simulated and when); the Metal testnet read (the mandate's state, not its cap; the cap is in the credential whose hash is on chain); the models per agent with the eval's numbers and the product's baseline row; the counters, their exact sentences and how the zero is computed; the test signer; the recorded runs and that code decides beside them. Rewrite the row that says the Worker's Airwallex client makes two calls (there are two clients and two tables now). The rows on `/try/sign` say its live agents moved to `/go`. Correct row 67 (the stale "Claude Haiku" sentence).
The runbook: the secrets by name and who sets them; the sandbox setup and the top-up; the deploy to staging and to production; the admin view; the day caps and the Demo Day overrides; making the event key and the QR code; the pre-ramp; "protect"; the fallbacks in order; rollback with the version id; the stage sentences the owner may say ("N scenarios played", "0 payments past a limit without a signature"; never "people", never "Face ID signatures").
Not claimed anywhere: that the demo books in T:0, files in a vault, touches Visa, reads the mandate's cap from the chain, or that a refusal of the visitor's own purchase happened on chain.
Tests first: the existing document tests (`test/first-screen.test.ts`, `test/submission.test.ts`, the claims and link checks) stay green or are updated in the same change with the sentence they pin.
Checks: `npm test`, the claims and link checks the repository has (`npm run verify` where it applies offline).
Out of scope: the video; the LinkedIn post.

title: Secrets, staging, production, rehearsals (with the owner)
spec:
Goal: the demo is live, capped and rehearsed, with a rollback ready. This task is a runbook carried out with the owner, not code.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §17, §12; docs/jury-demo/runbook.md.
Steps: (1) The owner confirms the Cloudflare plan is Workers Paid with a usage notification, and sets the secrets by hand: `JURY_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (a separate workspace with a spend limit of USD 80), `JURY_ADMIN_TOKEN` (at least 32 random bytes), `JURY_AWX_CLIENT_ID` and `JURY_AWX_API_KEY` (the dedicated sandbox key), `JURY_METAL_RPC_URL`. (2) Deploy the bundle to a staging Worker (`kit11-staging`, its own Durable Object, only the admin token as a secret); run the streaming smoke and `npm run jury:load` at 50, 150 and 300; write `docs/jury-demo/load.md`. (3) Note the production version id (`npx wrangler versions list` in `worker/`). Deploy with `JURY_DEMO_ENABLED=on TRY_SIGN_ENABLED=on npm run relay:deploy` on the owner's word. Nothing is live yet: the configuration is empty. (4) In the admin view: the caps of design §12.3 (first a day cap of USD 2), the models from the eval, the rail pool shares, the rail balance from the setup; then `live` on, then `rails_awx` and `rails_metal` on if the go or no-go said go. (5) `npx tsx test/browser/jury.check.ts --live`, `headers.check.ts --live`, `pages.check.ts --live`; read the Sonnet and Opus rate limits from the admin view into the runbook. (6) Three dress rehearsals with a stopwatch: an iPhone (Safari, Face ID), an Android phone (Chrome), a Mac (Touch ID), a Windows laptop, a security key, Firefox, one in-app browser, on 4G and Wi-Fi, and once from a corporate network; the median per device goes into the runbook, and "about 3 minutes" is printed only if the median first-time iPhone visit is at most 3:30. (7) Set the day caps for normal days; make the juror key and put its link into the submission form. (8) Freeze six hours before the submission; write the run record `docs/runs/2026-11-1x-jury-demo.md` (what ran live, ids, times, what was simulated).
Stop rules: any 5xx in the live checks, a counter that is not what the rehearsal did, a label that names a partner for work it did not do, or a payment without a signature row: switch `live` or the rail off, fix, redeploy.
Checks: the three live checks green; the admin view's spend equals the rehearsals' cost within a cent.
Out of scope: the Demo Day evening itself (the runbook's checklist); the videos.

title: After the submission: /go/count for the big screen, with event counters

title: After the submission: the cache warm-up and the pre-ramp before the QR moment
spec:
Goal: a crowd that starts at once meets warm caches and no sudden-increase limit.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §13, §17.
Files: `src/jury/desk/admin.ts` (op `warm {minutes, perMinute}`), `src/jury/agents/anthropic.ts` (`warmTurn(key: string, r: StreamRequest, f?: typeof fetch): Promise<{ ok: boolean; usage: Tokens | null }>`: the same tools, system, thinking and effort as real traffic, `max_tokens: 0`, not streamed), `src/jury/page/admin.ts` (a button), `test/jury-warm.test.ts`.
`warm` sends cache-refresh calls for the Checker, the Payer and the Sourcing agent (the Reader cannot be warmed this way: a structured output format refuses `max_tokens: 0`), ramping over the minutes given (default 3 minutes, from 20 to 300 a minute), inside the budget (each call is reserved and settled like any other, about USD 0.07 for 600 Sonnet calls), and stops when a lane closes.
Tests first: the request equals a real turn's except `max_tokens: 0` and no `stream`; the ramp's schedule with a fake clock; it stops on a closed lane and on a refused reserve; it is refused without the admin token.
Checks: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, the test file. One small deploy on the owner's word.
Out of scope: changing limits.

title: Stretch: Metal's own answer for the visitor's amount
spec:
Goal: row 3 of the overspend screen becomes Metal's own refusal reason, read live for this visitor's amount.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §2 (Mandate), §9.7; `node_modules/@metalntwx/metal-pay/dist/mandates/` (`buildL3a`, `signL3a`, `readCheck`, `REASONS`, `MANDATE_MAX_VALIDITY_SECONDS`).
Files: `src/cli/jurySandbox.ts` (subcommand `metal-checks`), `docs/demo/jury-sandbox.json` (`metal.checks`), `src/jury/rails/metal.ts` (`check(amount: string)`), `src/jury/scenario/world.ts` (the chain amount is drawn from the amounts that have a check), `test/jury-metal-check.test.ts`.
At setup, on a laptop with the demo agent's mandate key (it never goes into the Worker): for 24 over-cap amounts build and sign a payment under the demo mandate with the longest validity the contract accepts, encode the `check(pull, fields)` call data, and probe one with a read-only `eth_call`. Only if the answer is `OverPerPaymentCap` (and not `OutsideWindow`) write the 24 blobs into the sandbox file; otherwise write none and say why in the run record.
In the Worker: `check` sends one allowlisted blob with `eth_call` at the block just read and maps the returned number through `REASONS`. The screen then says: "Asked Metal's mandate contract, read-only, at block {n}: would it pay {amount}? Answer: mandate_cap_exceeded. Nothing was sent. The payment request was signed by the demo agent's key when the demo was set up." Any other answer falls back to the state read's wording.
Tests first: only allowlisted blobs are sent; the reason mapping; a blob that answers something else gives the fallback wording; no key in the sandbox file.
Checks: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, the test file.
Out of scope: binding or changing a mandate from the Worker.

title: Stretch: approve a catch invoice that came to the visitor

title: Stretch: open the visitor's own company in Purser Cloud
spec:
Goal: the summary's export opens as an ephemeral read-only company in the public Purser Cloud demo deployment.

title: Stretch: an own invoice, read and checked, never stored
spec:
Goal: a visitor drops their own invoice and watches the Reader and the Checker work on it, beside the scenario.
Context: docs/jury-demo/design.md §12.9.
Files: `src/jury/client/upload.ts`, `src/jury/desk/upload.ts` (endpoint `upload {token, text}`), `src/jury/copy.ts`, `test/jury-upload.test.ts`.
Rules: PDF, PNG or JPEG only, checked by the first bytes in the page; at most 2 MB and 3 pages; the text is taken in the page (the PDF's text layer; an image is not read: it gets "This demo reads text PDFs only."); only the text is sent, at most 20,000 characters, cleaned with `cleanText`; nothing is stored on the server and nothing is written to the chain; one upload a world; the Reader and the Checker run on it once, with an empty supplier file, inside the world's budget; the result is shown beside the scenario, labelled "your document, not part of this test world", and can never be signed, paid, booked or exported. Its text is data: it goes inside `<document>` tags, and `findInjections` (`src/policy/injection.ts`) marks planted instructions on screen.
Tests first: the type and size checks; a second upload is refused; the text is in no table after the visit; a document with planted instructions cannot change any tool input or outcome of the world; the upload cannot reach `sign`, `pay` or `export`.
Checks: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, the test file, `test/jury-redteam.test.ts`.
Out of scope: scans (no vision call).

title: Stretch: a 30-second tour and an anonymous feedback button

Feedback is three choices on the summary ("Clear", "Confusing", "Did not work"), stored only as three counters with no world id and no text, shown in the admin view.
Tests first: the copy's budgets; one feedback a world; nothing but the counter is stored.
Checks: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, the test file.
Out of scope: free-text feedback.
